23. DIABETES IN PREGNANCY

Pre conception counselling:

•Individualized dietary advice.
•Weight reduction if BMI >27.
•Folic acid 5mg till 12 weeks.
•Monthly HbA1C:
-Aim < 48 mol/ mol – 6.5%.
-C/I to pregnancy > 86mol/mol – 10%.

Stop other mediation pre – conceptionally.

•Retinal assessment (if not done within 6m0).
•Renal assessment (if not done within 6m0).

 

Referral to nephrologist:

1.Serum Creatinine > 1.2.
2.Albumin: Creatinine> 30 mg/nmol.
3.GFR < 45ml/min.

Gestational Diabetes:

R.F:

1.BMI > 30 screening @ 24 – 28 weeks.
2.Previous baby wight > 4.5k screening @ 24 – 28 weeks.
3.Previous GDM @ booking if normal then Repeat @ 24 – 28 weeks.
4.Family history screening @ 24 – 28 weeks.
5.Ethnicity screening @ 24 – 28 weeks.

Glycosuria:

•2+ on single event.
•1 + on 2 occasions

Indicate GDM

 

Further Testing OGTT.

OGTT:

•75g OGTT, 2hours duration
•At Booking (1st, 2nd ) – with previous GDM.
•24 – 28 with previous normal OGTT.

Fasting > 5. 6 GDM refer to joint Diabetes

2 hours > 7.8 clinic within 1 week of diagnosis

•Early self-monitoring – with previous history of GDM.

Interventions:

•Education:
-Fetomaternal risk.
-Benefit of controlled BSL.
-Self – monitoring of BSL.
-Diet and exercise (walking 30min after meal daily).
•Dietician Referral all women:
⇨Fasting BSL;

1.<7 mmol/ lit:

→Diet + exercise for 1 – 2 weeks.
→Start metformin if not controlled after 1 – 2 weeks of diet and exercise.
→Insulin if Metformin C/I or not tolerated.

2. ≥ 7 offer insulin + diet + exercise + Metformin.

3.6 – 6.9 + complications.

Consider insulin + diet + exercise.

4.Offer Glibenclamide if Metformin not effective/Not tolerated.

ANC:

•Joint diabetic + A/N clinic (1 – 2 weekly visits).

 

 

 

BSL Monitoring:

•Type 1
•Type 2 on multiple 4 levels:
•GDM daily dosage 1. Fasting

Regimen. 2. Pre-meal

3.Post-meal 1hr.

4. Bed time.

Type 2 on diet exercise

GDM oral therapy or

Single dose 2 levels:

insulin. 1. Fasting.

2. One hour - post meal.

 

 

 

Targets:

-Fasting – 5.3
-1 hour post meal – 7.8

-2 hours – 6.4.

Above 4mmol/lit.

HbA1C Monitoring:

•At booking – all women with pre – existing diabetes.
•Consider in 2nd and 3rd to assess risk/
•All women with GDM @ diagnosis.

Don’t measure to check the control.

Targets: <48 6.5%.

Hypoglycemia & insulin Treatment:

•Aspart/ Lispro – rapid acting – recommended during pregnancy.
•Explain hypoglycemia and treatment:
-Fasting acting glucose.
-Glucagon – type I.
•Offer continuous S/C insulin infusion.

If hypoglycemia + uncontrolled BSL with Multiple dosage.

• Continuous glucose monitoring:
-Don’t offer routinely.
-Offer:
⇨Problematic Hypoglycemia.
⇨Unstable BSL.
⇨To gain information about variability in BSL.

Ketone Monitoring/Testing:

•Type I:
-Offer strips & meter.
-Home testing if unwell or raised BSL
-Urgent help if ketones positive.
•Type II + GDM:
-Unwell or hyperglycemia | seek urgent help.

Urgent ketones

Positive ketones Admit level II.

Retinal Assessment:

•Offer in preexisting DM (if not done in previous 3m0).

@ booking.

@ 28 weeks.

•Pts with retinopathy @ booking (1 additional)

@ 16 – 20weeks again @ 28weeks.

@ 6months after child birth.

•Vaginal birth is not C/I in retinopathy.

Renal Assessment:

•Offer – (if not done in 3m0).
•Refer to nephrologist:

-Creatinine > 1.2
-Albumin: creatinine > 30mg/mol.
-Protein excretion > 0.5g/ day.
-Don’t use GFR.
•Thromboprophylaxis.
-Albumin: creatinine > 220mg/mol
-Proteinuria > 5g/day.

Fetal Monitoring:

•Anomaly Scan for structural anomalies + heart defects including:
-4 chambers.
-3 vessels.
-Out flaw track.

@20 weeks

Most common

VSD.

Pathognomonic:

Sacral agenesis.

•Growth + well-being: @

28, 32, 36 weeks including AFI

•Routine Doppler, BPP, CTG, not recommended.

IUGR + Growth Scan:

•Macro vascular disease.
•Nephropathy.
•Pre-eclampsia

IPC:

•Discuss with women:
-Timing of birth.
-Mode.
-Anaesthesia.

Type I + II:

•No other complications | 37 – 38 + 6 weeks.
•With fetal/ maternal or

metabolic complication | before 37 weeks.

GDM:

•No complications | - Before 40 + 6 weeks.

Elective birth if not delivered till 40 + 6 weeks.

•With complications | - Elective birth before 40+6 weeks.

Whenever complications arise.

Macrosomia on USG:

•Discuss with women:
-SVD.
-IOC.
-C/S.

Anaesthesia:

•Evaluation in 3rd .

If DM + comorbidities:

-Obesity.
-Neuropathy.

G.A:

•BSL every 30 min from induction of anesthesia till delivery of baby & women as conscious.

Regional Anaesthesia:

•BSL every 1 hour

BSL Monitoring During labour

•1 hourly (target 4 – 7 mmol/lit).

Insulin infusion - Type I – all women.

+ Dextrose. - Type II, GDM:

If BSL is not between 4 – 7 mmol/lit during labor.

 

 

Neonatal Care:

•Delivery in unit where resuscitation available during 24 hours.
•BSL level – 2 – 4hours after birth (routinely).
•Polycythemia, Hyper bilirubinemia if

Hypocalcemia, hypo magnesemia clinical signs

•Echo if clinical signs present
•Admissions:
-Hypoglycemia + abnormal signs.
-RDS + pre – term < 34 weeks.
-Cardiac signs.
-Encephalopathy.
-Polycythemia (partial exchange Tx).
-Need for I/V fluid or N – G feeding.
-Jaundice – requiring phototherapy.
•Hypoglycemia:
-Early feeding within 30 min – every 2 – 3 hours until BSL = 2mmol/lit.
1.Not effective feeding
2.Abnormal clinical signs. N – G feeding
3.< 2 mol on 2 reading or

Despite Max feeding. I/V dextrose.

Don’t Discharge before 24 hours.

PNC:

•Reduce insulin dose immediately after birth.
•Shift to pre pregnancy regimen or cut the dose up to 50% if it is diagnosed 1st time in pregnancy

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

GDM:

•Lifestyle modifications
-6 – 3 weeks post-natal fasting BSL.
-After 13 weeks – fasting BSL or HbA1C.

Fasting 6 or HbA1c < 39 = 5.7%.

⇨Low probability of DM @ present.
⇨Continue lifestyle modification
⇨Annual testing HbA1C.
⇨Moderate risk of type 2 DM

Fasting 6 – 6.9 or HbA1C 39 -47= 5.7 – 6.5%

⇨High risk of type 2 DM.
⇨Advice regarding prevention.

Fasting >7 or HbA1C > 48 = 6.5%.

Have DM type (2).
